September 30 Argon announcement was limited to trusted testers, so October 13 is a material access change.

google.reason: October 13 made Gemini 4 Argon available through the Gemini API after the September 30 limited-access announcement. The paid model ID and introductory price are documented; claims of performance remain vendor claims.

candidates.title: Gemini 4 Argon reaches the public Gemini API: evaluate a frontier model for complex coding tasks
candidates.summary: Google opened Gemini 4 Argon globally to developers and enterprises via the Gemini API on October 13, following a September 30 trusted-tester announcement. Builders can now compare it on a real complex coding task using the paid model ID gemini-4-argon.
candidates.availability: Public paid Gemini API; Google AI Pro/Ultra in the Gemini app; Google AI Ultra in Antigravity. Introductory API prices run through November 30. Access and safeguards vary by surface.
candidates.practical_use: Choose a representative multi-file coding task, evaluate Argon against an existing model using the same repository, instructions and review criteria, and inspect correctness and token cost before switching.

source_review.excerpt: now globally available to developers and enterprises via the Gemini API
source_review.decision: Read Google's October 13 launch, September 30 limited-access announcement and current API pricing. No live model call or independent benchmark performed.
source_review.availability: Paid Gemini API with model ID gemini-4-argon; app and Antigravity require separate Google AI subscription tiers.

candidates.title: OpenAI documents a Codex cleanup audit with GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol
candidates.summary: OpenAI published its own October 14 case study of Codex maintenance. In one internal stale-feature-flag audit, GPT-6.1 Sol Ultra found 131 reviewed findings at $15.12 API cost; GPT-6 Astra Ultra found 142 at $109.06. Sol missed some flags used as dependencies. These are one team's results, not a general benchmark.
candidates.availability: Codex with an available GPT-6 Astra or GPT-6.1 Sol model and permission to inspect the target repository; external configuration and production telemetry require separately authorized access.
candidates.practical_use: Audit one small stale flag or unused-code area, require evidence before proposing removal, preserve kill switches, and compare accepted findings and cost across model/effort settings on the same repository snapshot.

source_review.excerpt: GPT-6.1 Sol Ultra produced 92% as many findings as GPT-6 Astra Ultra at 14% of the API cost.
source_review.decision: Read OpenAI's October 14 case study and its methods, reviewed findings, costs and missed dependency pattern. Attribute all measurements to OpenAI's internal audit; no independent Codex run performed.
source_review.availability: The described workflow requires Codex model access plus permission to inspect repository history and any external flags or telemetry; this channel did not access OpenAI internal systems.
